questions.q: On the balance beam, relative weights 20, 50 and 10 sit at $x = 1, 5, 9$. Where is the balance point $E[X]$?
questions.explain: $E[X] = \frac{20 \cdot 1 + 50 \cdot 5 + 10 \cdot 9}{20 + 50 + 10} = \frac{360}{80} = 4.5$. Weights must be normalized into probabilities; $5$ is just the most likely outcome (the mode).

questions.q: Casino game: cost \$10, jackpot \$100, win probability 5%. Using $E[X] = P(\text{Win})(\text{Prize} - \text{Cost}) + P(\text{Lose})(-\text{Cost})$, what is the player's expected value per play?
questions.explain: $0.05 \times 90 + 0.95 \times (-10) = 4.5 - 9.5 = -5$. The house wins \$5 per play on average, even though individual players sometimes win big.

questions.q: Which statement about expected value is correct?
options: $E[X]$ is always one of the possible outcomes
$E[X]$ is the most likely single outcome
A positive $E[X]$ guarantees you win on every play
$E[X]$ is a probability-weighted average — the long-run average per trial — and need not be a possible outcome
questions.explain: E.g. the balance point 4.5 is not any of $1, 5, 9$. Over many plays the average per play settles toward $E[X]$, but short runs can stray far from it.

questions.q: A regression network trained with squared-error loss predicts which summary of the target distribution?
questions.explain: Minimizing average squared error is achieved by predicting the mean $E[Y \mid x]$. A classifier, in contrast, usually picks the single most likely class.
